mnemonic: A stunt rider is asked whether he can clear the canyon. He gives a thumbs-up — "dâi" — the same sound as DIE, which is exactly what the crowd behind him expects. He can, and he does. Dâi is the can, the got, the managed-it. (↓ falling, the thumb comes down as the engine opens up)
headline: dâi!
scene: A helmeted stunt rider on a motorbike balanced at the lip of a wide desert canyon, giving a confident thumbs-up back over his shoulder to a small crowd of horrified onlookers with their hands on their heads. A timber ramp waits ahead of him. Dust, hard midday sun.

mnemonic: A receptionist ends every sentence with a small dip of the head, and every dip carries the same soft sound: "cah", car with the R swallowed. Women hang it on the end of a statement the way the head dips. Leave it off and the sentence lands bare. (↓ falling, the head drops with the voice)
headline: …kâ.
scene: A hotel receptionist in a neat uniform standing behind a marble desk, head bowed and palms pressed together toward a guest she is handing a key to. Her whole posture is a small polite dip. Bright lobby, orchids on the counter, morning light through tall glass.

mnemonic: A queue of dancers waits at an audition and the director asks who is next. Every finger in the line swings toward one woman, and she points back at her own chest — "chǎn?" — me. Chǎn is I, the one being pointed at. (↑ rising, the finger and the voice go up together)
headline: Chǎn?
scene: A line of dancers waiting along a bare rehearsal-room wall, all of them pointing sideways at one woman near the middle, who has turned and is pointing back at her own chest with both hands, eyebrows up. Mirrored wall, scuffed floor, hard rehearsal lighting.

mnemonic: Everyone leaving the beach bar waves at the barmaid on their way out: "bye, Dee." She is comfortable, she is good, and she answers without lifting her head out of the hammock. Sà-baai-dii is sabai plus dii — comfortable-good, the standard answer to how are you. (— the last syllable lands flat and easy, nothing wrong at all)
headline: Bye, Dee!
scene: A barmaid lying back in a hammock strung behind a bamboo beach bar, one hand raised in a lazy wave, eyes closed and smiling. Two customers walk away down the sand waving back over their shoulders. Late gold light, flat turquoise sea, glasses left on the counter.

mnemonic: A toddler reaches for the cake and his grandmother's hand comes down flat over it: "mâi!" It is the same MY as the question word ไหม, but slammed down instead of lifted up. Not, no, don't. The tone does all the work. (↓ falling, the hand and the voice drop together)
headline: Mâi!
scene: A kitchen table with a whole iced cake on it. A small boy on tiptoe stretches for the edge of the plate while an old woman's hand lands flat across the top of the cake, her other hand raised. Her face is stern and amused at once. Warm afternoon light.

mnemonic: Two words the learner already has: tham, to do, and ngaan, the job. A clerk presses his inked thumb onto form after form, one for every hour of the shift, and the pile never gets smaller. Doing the job: tham-ngaan, to work. (— both syllables flat, the same stamp over and over)
headline: tham-ngaan.
scene: A tired clerk at a government desk pressing his inked thumb onto a sheet from a tower of identical forms, another tower already done beside him. Ink pad, worn wooden counter, a queue of people blurred behind the glass. Strip lighting, late afternoon.

mnemonic: A glass lift climbs the outside of a tower and the numbers climb with it. Say KOON but grinning, lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward, and you land kʰɯ̂n: up, to rise, to increase. Prices do it, rivers do it, buses are boarded with it. (↓ falling, though everything in the scene is going up)
headline: kʰɯ̂n!
scene: A glass lift rising up the outside of a tall office tower, seen from below, with two passengers inside looking out and down. The city shrinks beneath them, rooftops and wires. Bright hazy sky, sun flaring off the glass.

mnemonic: A man called Jack turns up at the door with a battered suitcase plastered in shipping labels from a dozen countries. Where is he from? All of it. Jàak marks where a thing comes from — the starting point, never the destination. (▁ low and flat, a plain statement of origin)
headline: jàak.
scene: A traveller standing on a wooden doorstep at dusk with a battered leather suitcase bound in rope and worn straps, hat in hand, rain on his shoulders. The door is opening, warm light spilling onto him. A quiet street behind.

mnemonic: A woman steps up into the train, turns and waves — bye — and the doors close on her. Every leaving is a bye: bpai is to go, to head off, the direction away from where you are standing. (— flat and level, the wave held steady as the train pulls out)
headline: bpai.
scene: A woman standing in the open doorway of a departing train, one arm raised in a wave, bag over her shoulder. On the platform a small group waves back through the steam and motion blur. Overhead station lights, early morning.

mnemonic: A train guard cannot remember a single passenger's name, so he just points and goes "choo" — lips pulled wide in a grin rather than pushed forward, which is exactly the Thai vowel. Chɯ̂ɯ is the name, the thing you are asked for first. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the name lands)
headline: chɯ̂ɯ?
scene: A uniformed train guard walking a crowded carriage, pointing cheerfully at one seated passenger after another, mouth stretched wide in an odd grin. Passengers grin back, baffled. Wooden seats, luggage racks, sunlight strobing through the windows.

mnemonic: A gecko on a branch shoots its tongue out and the fly is gone. The tongue reaches, and it always gets there. Tʰɯ̌ng is arriving, reaching the place you were headed — and the point a thing extends to. (↑ rising, the flick goes up and out)
headline: tʰɯ̌ng!
scene: A green gecko clinging to a branch with its tongue shot out to full length toward a fly hovering just beyond, caught at the instant of contact. Broad tropical leaves, dappled light, shallow depth of field.

mnemonic: A boy at the breakfast table tips the entire jar of orange Tang powder into one glass — not some of it, the lot. Tʰáng is the whole thing, both halves, every last one. (▲ high and taut, the voice stays up like the upended jar)
headline: tʰáng!
scene: A kitchen table at breakfast. A boy holds an enormous jar upside down over a single tall glass, orange powder pouring out and clouding the air around him. Cereal bowls forgotten. Morning light, curtains, an unimpressed cat on a chair.

mnemonic: Two words already in the bag: thîi, the place, and yùu, to be living there. The place you live is your address. A postman holds up a parcel at the mouth of the lane and asks only that, and the whole street points at one gate. (▁ the second syllable settles low, fixed to the ground)
headline: thîi-yùu?
scene: A postman standing at the mouth of a narrow residential lane holding a brown parcel up in one hand. Four neighbours on doorsteps and balconies all point toward the same green gate further down. Washing lines, scooters, hot flat light.

mnemonic: The contract is signed, everyone is smiling — but then the lawyer tears the last page clean off. Tɛ̀ɛ is that tear: everything before it stands, and what comes after changes it. Say it like 'tear' with the R swallowed. (▁ low and flat, the paper comes away without drama)
headline: tɛ̀ɛ…
scene: A boardroom. A lawyer stands at the head of the table calmly ripping the bottom sheet off a stapled contract, the torn strip already curling. Three people around the table, smiles frozen, one half out of a chair. Glass wall, city behind, cold light.

mnemonic: Someone asks the farmer what happened after the storm. He holds up an apple core, shrugs, and that is the answer: so, then, that is how it went. Kɔ̂ɔ is the small hinge between one thing and the next. (↓ falling, the shoulders come down with the voice)
headline: kɔ̂ɔ…
scene: A farmer standing in a wrecked orchard holding up a bare apple core between finger and thumb, shoulders lifted in a shrug. Snapped branches and scattered fruit across the mud behind him. Grey light after rain.

mnemonic: Offer a Thai friend three restaurants and you will get kɔ̂ɔ-dâi — then-can, meaning any of them will do. It is the hinge word kɔ̂ɔ plus the can word dâi, delivered with the palms up. Agreement without enthusiasm, and it is everywhere. (↓ the second syllable drops, the shoulders drop with it)
headline: kɔ̂ɔ dâi.
scene: Three friends stopped on a street corner between three lit restaurant doorways. Two of them look expectantly at the third, who stands with both palms turned up and shoulders raised, entirely unbothered. Evening, neon reflections on wet pavement.

mnemonic: The place word thîi plus the knee of นี้ — this place. A man on a picnic blanket taps his own knee, then the grass right beside it: here, not over there, right at the knee. (↓ both syllables drop, each one planted)
headline: thîi-nîi.
scene: A man sitting cross-legged on a picnic blanket in a park, tapping his own knee with one hand and pressing his other flat on the grass beside the blanket. A friend standing a few metres away holds a basket, hesitating. Dappled shade, late morning.

mnemonic: A tea seller sets out two jars, one dark and one pale, and asks which yang you want. Every yin has its yang; every thing has its yàang — its sort, its kind, its type. (▁ low and flat, a plain sorting question)
headline: yàang nǎi?
scene: A tea seller behind a narrow counter with two open glass jars in front of her, one full of dark twisted leaves, one full of pale curled ones, holding a palm out over each. Shelves of jars behind, warm shop light, a customer's shoulder in frame.

mnemonic: Two baskets of flatbread on the counter. The customer waves off the near one and jabs a finger at the far basket — nán — that naan, the one over there. Níi is this; nán is that. (▲ high and taut, the finger jabs at arm's length)
headline: nán!
scene: A bakery counter with two wicker baskets of flatbread, one close and one at the far end. A customer leans across, waving one hand dismissively at the near basket while jabbing a finger at the far one. The baker looks along her arm. Flour dust, warm ovens.

mnemonic: The bartender fills the glass up to the red mark on its side and then keeps pouring. That mark is the limit; mâak is everything above it. Good, mâak. Hot, mâak. It is the word for too much of anything. (↓ falling, the pour keeps coming as the voice drops)
headline: mâak!
scene: A tall measuring glass on a bar with a red line ringing it partway up, liquid pouring over the rim and spreading across the counter. A bartender holds the bottle steady, looking straight at the viewer. Bottles behind, low amber light.

mnemonic: A baby cries somewhere in a dark house and every adult sits up in bed with the same question. Khrai sounds exactly like that cry, and the cry is always the question: whose baby, who is there, who did it. (— flat and level, the question sits in the middle)
headline: khrai?
scene: A dark bedroom, a couple sitting bolt upright in bed, both turned toward a half-open door with a strip of hallway light across the floor. Bedding thrown back, alarm clock on the nightstand. Deep blue night, one warm slice of light.

mnemonic: The vendor names a price so small that the shopper has already walked off with the shirt. It took almost nothing. Thùuk is cheap — and, awkwardly for the learner, also correct. (▁ low and flat, a short blunt word for a short blunt price)
headline: thùuk.
scene: A clothes stall in a covered market. A shopper walks away with a folded shirt under his arm, already several steps gone, while the vendor stands with one open palm holding a single small coin. Hanging garments, strip lights, crowded aisle.

mnemonic: A kangaroo at a fork in the path, one carrot in each paw, head tilting from side to side and unable to settle it. Say 'roo' with the lips spread flat and you have rɯ̌ɯ — the little word that puts two things side by side: this, or that. (↑ rising, the voice tilts up like the head)
headline: rɯ̌ɯ?
scene: A kangaroo standing upright at a fork in a dusty path, a carrot held in each front paw, head tipped to one side. Two tracks lead away into dry scrub. Low sun, long shadows, red dust.

mnemonic: The two-tone siren says it over and over as the ambulance carves through traffic: way-laa, way-laa. Every second it loses is time somebody has not got. Weelaa is time itself — the hour, the while, the when. (— both syllables flat and even, the siren holding its note)
headline: way-laa, way-laa
scene: An ambulance cutting between stopped cars on a wet city street at night, blue light smeared across the windscreens around it. A clock tower stands lit above the rooftops behind. Rain, headlights, motion blur.

mnemonic: The foreman watches the machine cough into life, sticks his thumb up, and the whole line starts moving. Tham is the doing word — make, do, get it done — and whatever the job is, the thumb settles it. (— flat and level, no fuss in it)
headline: tham.
scene: A factory floor. A foreman in a hard hat stands beside a starting conveyor with his thumb raised toward a control booth above. Workers along the line reach for the first parts coming through. Cold overhead lighting, oil-stained concrete.

mnemonic: A woman comes to her back door and finds a hen where no hen should be: up on the kitchen table, mid-strut, among the breakfast plates. Her chin lifts as she says it — hěn, I see it. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the eyebrows)
headline: hěn!
scene: A kitchen seen from the back doorway. A brown hen stands on the table stepping between plates and a teapot. A woman in the doorway has stopped dead, hands still on the door frame, chin up. Morning light across the floor tiles.

mnemonic: In the stairwell of an old hotel a chandelier hangs at every landing, one to a floor, each a little grander as you climb. Chán is the floor you are standing on — and, in a shop, the shelf. (▲ high and taut, said with the head tipped back)
headline: chán.
scene: Looking straight up a square hotel stairwell through four or five storeys of banisters, a lit chandelier hanging at each landing, the highest ones small with distance. Gilt, dust, warm bulbs against dark wood.

mnemonic: The type word yàang plus rai, what: what way? A cook is asked how she gets the noodles to fly like that and simply holds her wrist up mid-toss. Yàang-rai is how — the manner of doing a thing. (— the second syllable levels out, the question left hanging)
headline: yàang-rai?
scene: A street kitchen. A cook holds a wok up and away from the flame with noodles and beansprouts in mid-air above it, her wrist cocked. An apprentice stares from the side, his own wok untouched. Night market lights, fire, steam.

mnemonic: A farmer walks back across the field at dusk toward the one building with a light in it — the barn where everyone is waiting. Bâan is not the structure so much as the home inside it. (↓ falling, the voice settles the way he does)
headline: bâan.
scene: A farmer crossing a harvested field at dusk, silhouetted, tools over one shoulder, walking toward a low wooden house with one lit window and an open door. Hills and a fading orange sky behind. Long shadows across the stubble.

mnemonic: Given a mountain of vegetables to get through, the chef grins and reaches for the cleaver — chop, chop, chop, all afternoon — because this is the part of the job she likes. Chɔ̂ɔp is liking a thing enough to choose it. (↓ falling, the blade comes down with the voice)
headline: chɔ̂ɔp!
scene: A restaurant prep kitchen. A chef mid-swing with a heavy cleaver over a board heaped with spring onions, a vast crate of vegetables beside her, grinning. Chopped piles fan out across the steel counter. Steam and hard kitchen light.

mnemonic: The choirmaster stops the choir to fix the line which they have just sung — and that little 'which' is the word. Say SUNG with the lips spread flat instead of rounded and you have sɯ̂ng: the joiner that hooks a description onto whatever came before. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the clause attaches)
headline: sɯ̂ng…
scene: A choirmaster with one hand raised flat, having just cut off a choir mid-phrase; thirty singers stand with mouths still open. A church hall, high windows, folded music stands. Cool daylight from above.

mnemonic: A road crew stands over a steaming bucket of tar with the rain coming in. If they pour now it sets; if they wait they lose the day. Everything hangs on that if — thâa, said like 'tar' with the R swallowed. (↓ falling, the word drops like the first raindrop)
headline: thâa…
scene: Three road workers in overalls standing around a steaming black tar bucket on a half-finished stretch of road, all looking up at a bank of dark cloud rolling in. Rollers and cones behind them. First drops darkening the asphalt.

mnemonic: The stall keeps the same leaves and pours a third round from them, because nothing here is finished until it cannot be used again. Chái is to use — to put a thing to work. (▲ high and taut, a brisk working word)
headline: chái.
scene: A roadside tea stall. A vendor pours from a battered dented pot into a glass, the spent leaves heaped in a strainer beside her, three used glasses waiting. Close crop on hands and steam, sunlit street beyond.

mnemonic: A mare stands square over her foal in the paddock and will not let anyone past her shoulder. Say 'mare' with the R swallowed and you have mɛ̂ɛ — mother, and the first word a Thai child shouts. (↓ falling, the voice drops warm and final)
headline: mɛ̂ɛ.
scene: A chestnut mare standing broadside over a folded-up foal in wet paddock grass, ears back, head turned toward the fence. A figure at the gate has stopped with one hand on the latch. Morning mist, low sun.

mnemonic: A drummer walks down the lane beating a tom-tom and by the end of it every child in the village has fallen in behind him, matching his step. Taam is to follow — a person, a road, or a rule. (— flat and even, like the beat he keeps)
headline: taam!
scene: A drummer walking away down a narrow village lane with a tom-tom strapped at his hip, a straggling line of small children following in step behind him. Wooden houses, chickens scattering, dust and warm afternoon light.

mnemonic: Stick a hum on the front of 'earn' and you have it: ngɤɤn. At closing time the stallholder counts the day's takings into a biscuit tin, note by note. What she earned is what the word means — money, and silver before that. (— flat and level, coin after coin)
headline: ngɤɤn.
scene: A market stall after closing, shutters half down. A woman sits on a stool counting banknotes into a battered biscuit tin on her lap, coins stacked on the counter beside her. One hanging bulb, everything else dark.

mnemonic: A row of balloons tied along a fence, and only some of them go bang — three burst, the rest hang there untouched. Baang is exactly that: some, certain ones, not all of them. (— flat and level, no drama in the word itself)
headline: baang.
scene: A garden fence strung with a row of party balloons, three of them burst into curls of rubber on their strings, the rest still full and bobbing. Trestle table with paper cups behind. Bright afternoon, grass, no people.

mnemonic: Do plus give: tham (to do) and hâi (to give). A father tickles a baby until she shrieks with laughter — he did something, and it gave her the laugh. That is the whole word: this made that happen. (↓ the second syllable drops, the handing-over)
headline: tham-hâi.
scene: A father sitting on the floor with a baby lying across his knees, both hands tickling her ribs, both of them mid-laugh with eyes screwed shut. Sunlit living room, scattered toys, curtains moving.

mnemonic: A boy snatches a roasting chestnut straight off the brazier — ow — and hangs on to it anyway, because he wants it. Ao is wanting and taking in one syllable, and the vendor will throw it at you as a question. (— flat and level, said fast)
headline: ao!
scene: A street brazier of chestnuts glowing over coals. A small boy has just grabbed one and is shaking his hand in the air, chestnut clamped in his fingers, face screwed up. The vendor leans back laughing. Night, sparks, orange light.

skip_reason: No honest English anchor for aa-hǎan: 'ah-harn' is not a word and reaching for 'harness' adds a pun chain without teaching the vowel.

mnemonic: The hunter presses his ear flat to the coffin lid with the fangs an inch away on the other side. Listening is the entire job. Fang is to listen, and it is the English word unchanged. (— flat and level, held completely still)
headline: fang.
scene: A stone crypt lit by one candle. A man kneels with his ear pressed against the lid of a heavy wooden coffin, eyes wide, both palms flat on the wood. Cobwebs, damp walls, a single flame.

mnemonic: Three friends order; two have chosen and the third is still reading. The waitress turns to her with one eyebrow up and a single syllable: khun lâ — and you? Lâ is the nudge that throws the question back at someone. (↓ falling, the voice drops as the eyebrow goes up)
headline: khun lâ?
scene: A restaurant table of three. A waitress with a notepad has turned to the last diner, pen poised, one eyebrow raised. Two friends watch the third, who is still hidden behind a tall folded card held up to her face. Warm interior, low pendant lights.

mnemonic: A baker's tray of identical round baps with one plaited loaf among them — a different bɛ̀ɛp, the same dough. Bɛ̀ɛp is the model, the kind, the way a thing is made or worn. (▁ low and flat, a plain word for a plain thing)
headline: bɛ̀ɛp nǎi?
scene: A bakery window tray packed with identical round bread rolls, one plaited loaf sitting among them, slightly larger. Flour on the tray, tongs resting on the edge, a child's face reflected in the glass. Morning light.

mnemonic: The place word thîi plus sùt, the end: the point right at the end of the line. A sweep climbs out on top of the tallest chimney in the city, black with soot, every other stack below him. The most, the -est of anything. (▁ the last syllable drops low and stops)
headline: thîi-sùt.
scene: A chimney sweep sitting astride the rim of the tallest brick chimney above a city of smaller stacks and rooftops, soot-blackened, brushes slung on his back. Smoke drifting below him. Cold dawn, pale sky.

mnemonic: Every cake on the stand sits on its own lace doily, and each doily was cut by hand by the woman behind the counter — made by her. Dooi is the by-word: done by, through, by means of. (— flat and level, a quiet credit)
headline: dooi.
scene: A glass-fronted cake stand. A woman's hands lower a small iced cake onto a white lace doily on the top shelf, a stack of cut doilies beside her. Scissors and paper scraps on the counter. Bright shop light.

mnemonic: A man upends the entire sofa hunting for his keys, and when they finally drop out of the frame he says the word itself — hǎa. The looking and the finding share one sound. (↑ rising, the voice climbs the longer the search goes on)
headline: hǎa!
scene: A living room turned over: a sofa tipped upside down, cushions everywhere, a man on his knees underneath it with one arm out to catch a set of keys falling from the frame. Lamp knocked sideways, evening light.

mnemonic: One hen finds the split feed sack and immediately tells the whole yard about it — bawk, bawk, bawk — until every bird in the place is running. Bɔ̀ɔk is to tell: news, instructions, or the truth. (▁ low and flat, a plain announcement)
headline: bɔ̀ɔk.
scene: A farmyard. One hen stands on a burst sack of grain with her beak open mid-squawk, wings half spread, while a dozen other hens sprint toward her from every corner. Spilled feed, straw, hard morning light.

mnemonic: A man who sued for damages settles out of court and has spent the cheque by the afternoon. Say 'sue' with the lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward and you land sɯ́ɯ — to buy. (▲ high and taut, the word snaps up like a price)
headline: sɯ́ɯ!
scene: A man in a crumpled suit walking down courthouse steps loaded with shopping bags in both hands, a new hat on, grinning. Pigeons, columns, other people in suits going the other way. Bright midday.

mnemonic: Four friends outside a karaoke bar and one of them still hesitating on the step. The others tug his sleeve: pai thə̀ — go on, let's. It is the softest possible shove, the syllable that turns an order into a let's. (▁ low and short, gone almost before it starts)
headline: pai thə̀!
scene: A neon karaoke doorway at night. Three young people have hold of a fourth by the sleeve and elbow, hauling him laughing toward the entrance while he leans back. Wet pavement, reflected neon, scooters parked along the kerb.

mnemonic: The one Thai particle that translates itself: jâ is ja, the German yes, and it carries the same warm agreement — an aunt answering a small child, a friend saying of course. Women use it where the conversation is friendly rather than formal. (↓ falling, warm and settled)
headline: jâ.
scene: A kitchen doorway. An aunt in an apron leans down nodding at a small child who is holding up an empty bowl with both hands. Steam from a pot behind her, worn tiles, warm afternoon light.

mnemonic: One letter short of เพื่อน, friend — and that is the sense: pʰɯ̂a is doing a thing for somebody, and adding the n gives you the person you do it for. The vowel is the hard part: start at 'oo' with the lips spread flat and let it fall away into 'ah'. (↓ falling, the voice drops like something handed over)
headline: pʰɯ̂a khun.
scene: Two women walking a rainy street under one umbrella, the nearer one holding it entirely over her friend so that her own shoulder and sleeve are soaked through. Puddles, passing headlights, evening.

mnemonic: A temple bell is struck once for every year of the old abbot's life, and a novice keeps count with knots in a cord — each time it rang, one more knot. Khráng is that: a time, an occasion, once. (▲ high and taut, the note hanging in the air)
headline: khráng.
scene: A young monk standing beside a huge bronze temple bell, a knotted cord looped through his fingers, the swinging beam just leaving the bell's rim. Other monks watching from the steps. Early gold light, incense smoke.

mnemonic: Asked whether the mangoes will be ripe by Friday, the farmer looks up at the tree, tips his hand from side to side and says máng — probably, don't hold me to it. The first syllable of mango, thrown up high. (▲ high, the voice lifts and leaves it open)
headline: máng.
scene: A mango orchard. A farmer stands under a heavy tree of half-ripe fruit, one hand tipping side to side at chest height, squinting up. A buyer beside him with an empty crate waits. Hot hazy light through leaves.

mnemonic: One lie needs a second one to prop it up, and that one needs three more. By midnight he has lǎai of them — many, more than he can keep straight. (↑ rising, the voice climbs with the pile)
headline: lǎai.
scene: A man sitting on the edge of his bed in the small hours, head in his hands, the floor around him buried under a huge drift of crumpled paper balls. One lamp, curtains drawn, everything else dark.

mnemonic: A tray of sweets goes round the classroom and each child takes exactly one — took, took, took, all the way along the row. Thúk is every and each, one at a time, and it is short: took, not toooook. (▲ high and taut, clipped off)
headline: thúk khon.
scene: A classroom row seen along its length: a tray of wrapped sweets being passed hand to hand, each child holding one already, the last two reaching. Wooden desks, uniforms, sunlight through louvred windows.

mnemonic: Point at the line snaking along the railings outside the embassy and ask what it is: that is a queue. Say 'queue' with the lips spread flat rather than pushed forward and you have kʰɯɯ — the equals sign of Thai: this is that. (— flat and level, stating a fact)
headline: khɯɯ…
scene: A long queue of people along iron railings outside a grand stone building, doubling back on itself. A newcomer stands at the end pointing along it with a puzzled expression. Grey morning, coats, bags.

mnemonic: A green shoot breaks the crust of a cracked field: everything that is born comes up out of the dirt. Gɤ̀ɤt rhymes with dirt with a hard G on the front — to be born, to arise, to happen at all. (▁ low and flat, the first quiet moment of a life)
headline: gɤ̀ɤt.
scene: Close view of a single green seedling pushing up through hard cracked earth, soil crumbs lifted on its bent head. A wide dry field blurred behind. First light, long low shadows.

mnemonic: Put a hum in front of 'naan' and you have it. The baker slaps flatbread onto the oven wall all night — this is his ngaan, his work. A wedding or a fair is a ngaan too: any event people work at. (— flat and level, the same all shift)
headline: ngaan.
scene: A tandoor oven glowing with coals, a baker leaning in to slap a disc of dough against the hot clay wall, several breads already stuck and blistering. Bare arms, flour, sweat, deep night behind him.

mnemonic: A stallholder sets a heavy jar of orange Tang down on the trestle at dawn and it stands there all day. That is tâng: to set a thing up and leave it standing. Careful — tʰáng with the voice held high is 'all'. (↓ falling, the jar comes down with the voice)
headline: tâng.
scene: Two hands lowering a heavy glass jar of orange powder onto a wooden trestle table at a market, the wood bowing slightly. Other stalls stretch away unopened behind. Early light, empty aisles.

mnemonic: A rap on the door, and the man opens it to a courier holding out a parcel. He takes it, both hands. Ráp is to receive — a parcel, a guest, a phone call, a job. (▲ high and taut, quick as the knock)
headline: ráp.
scene: A front door half open. A courier on the step holds out a brown parcel; the householder has both hands on it, taking the weight. Van at the kerb behind, rain on the path, grey afternoon.

mnemonic: The first tray out of the oven goes onto the top rack, too hot to touch, while the window is still dark. Stretch it — raaack — and you have rɛ̂ɛk: the first one, the first time. (↓ falling, the tray lands)
headline: rɛ̂ɛk.
scene: A bakery before dawn. A baker slides a tray of pale rolls onto the top shelf of a tall steel cooling rack, every shelf below it empty. Dark window, flour dust in the lamplight.

mnemonic: Two people stand in front of a canvas of splashes with their heads tilted. It might be art. It might not. Àat is exactly that hedge — may, might, possibly — said like 'art' with the R swallowed. (▁ low and flat, no commitment in the voice)
headline: àat.
scene: A white gallery wall with one enormous splattered canvas. Two visitors stand well back with their heads tilted at the same angle, one with a hand on his chin. Spotlights, polished concrete floor.

mnemonic: Ask for a different room and the clerk turns to the board of hanging keys for another one. Say 'oon' with the lips spread flat, not pushed forward, and you have ɯ̀ɯn: the other one, some other, a different one from this. (▁ low and flat, a plain alternative)
headline: ʔɯ̀ɯn.
scene: A small hotel desk. A clerk reaches up to a board of keys hanging on hooks, one hand on a key, while a guest waits with a bag at her feet. A brass bell and a vase of flowers on the counter, dim lobby beyond.

mnemonic: First morning of a new term: the bell goes, the gates swing open and a hundred children pour through at once. Rɤ̂ɤm rhymes with term, and a term is the thing that starts. (↓ falling, the bell drops into the yard)
headline: rɤ̂ɤm!
scene: School gates swinging inward with a crowd of uniformed children surging through into a yard, bags swinging, a teacher standing to one side. Long shadows, low morning sun, dust in the air.

mnemonic: A small boy has claimed the rail at the stern of the ferry and is shouting at the wake. The deck is his. Dèk is a child — short, blunt and low, like the boards under his feet. (▁ low and flat, a short stamp of a word)
headline: dèk.
scene: The stern deck of a wooden ferry. A small boy grips the rail and leans out over the churning white wake, mouth open, hair flat in the wind. Passengers sit behind him in the shade. Bright glare off the water.

mnemonic: A boy stands rigid against the door frame while his mother lays her hand flat on his head and marks the wood. Taller soon, taller again soon, the marks climbing every year. Sǔung is high, tall, the top end of anything. (↑ rising, like the marks going up the frame)
headline: sǔung!
scene: A kitchen door frame covered in short pencil marks at different heights. A boy stands hard against it on tiptoe while his mother presses one hand flat on his head and reaches with a pencil. Warm hallway light.

mnemonic: He gets to the buffet one minute late and the tray is already gone. He should have come before. Gɔ̀ɔn is before, first, ahead of the other thing. (▁ low and flat, the word lands after the fact)
headline: gɔ̀ɔn.
scene: A function hall after the rush. A man in a suit stares down at an empty steel serving tray with tongs lying across it, crumbs and a smear of sauce left. Stacked chairs, other emptied trays, cold strip lighting.

mnemonic: Two cooks taste from the same pot and disagree: one gets a sharp citrus tang, the other gets nothing at all. Different tongues, different tàang. Tàang is different, other, not the same. (▁ low and flat, said with a shrug)
headline: tàang.
scene: Two cooks either side of a steaming stockpot, each with a tasting spoon halfway to their mouth. One is wincing hard, the other shrugging with eyebrows raised. Steel kitchen, steam, overhead lamps.

skip_reason: Three-syllable formal word with no honest English anchor; phan-rá-yaa maps to nothing a learner already knows, and the existing entry is a bare restatement.

mnemonic: Ràp, to receive, is sitting inside it: sǎm-ràp marks whoever receives the thing. A boy hands over a brown-paper parcel wrapped for a man named Sam — Sam-rap — and it is for him, nobody else. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the parcel changes hands)
headline: sǎm-ràp Sam.
scene: A boy on a doorstep holding out a brown-paper parcel tied with string to a man who has both hands on it. Neither has let go. Terrace houses, milk bottles on the step, flat morning light.

mnemonic: The bell in the middle of the square is the one that clangs, and every lane in the town runs to it. Klaang is the middle, the centre — and the clang comes from exactly there. (— flat and level, the note held)
headline: klaang.
scene: A high view of a village square with a small open bell tower at its dead centre, four lanes running out from it between tiled roofs. A man swinging the bell rope below. Midday, short shadows.

mnemonic: The one who is locked out knocks; the one inside opens. A knock always comes from nɔ̂ɔk — outside, out of, beyond the door. Nɔ̂ɔk is everything past the threshold. (↓ falling, the fist comes down)
headline: nɔ̂ɔk.
scene: A wooden door seen from the wet street, a fist mid-knock against it, rain running off a coat sleeve. Warm light in the window beside the door and a shape moving behind the glass. Night.

mnemonic: You already say this one: Mɯang Thai, the Thai country — literally the Thai city. A mɯang is a town, and the old kingdoms were single walled towns with their fields around them. Say it 'moo-ang' with the lips spread flat. (— flat and level, both parts even)
headline: mɯang thai
scene: An old walled town seen from a hillside: a moat and brick rampart enclosing tiled temple roofs and lanes, with rice paddies and palms spreading out beyond the wall. Hazy hills on the horizon, warm late light.

mnemonic: A busker will sing about anything you drop in his hat — a spanner, an apple, somebody's lost glove. Every one of them is a sìng: a thing, any thing at all. (▁ low and flat, the most ordinary word there is)
headline: sìng.
scene: A street busker with a guitar mid-song, an upturned hat at his feet holding a spanner, an apple and a single glove instead of coins. Two passers-by grinning. Shopfronts, pavement, afternoon light.

mnemonic: The leader of the race comes round the bend alone with the camera bike ahead of him and the pack nowhere in sight. Nam is 'num' with the rest of number cut off: to lead, to take the front, to bring others along. (— flat and level, an even pace)
headline: nam.
scene: A lone marathon runner on an empty road coming round a bend, a motorcycle with a camera rig just ahead of him, crowds pressed against barriers on both sides. Wet tarmac, grey morning.

mnemonic: The fridge dies in the night and the whole tray of prawns has turned. She holds one up at arm's length, pulls a face and drops it in the bin: see-ya. Sǐa is spoiled, wasted, broken, gone bad. (↑ rising, the voice lifts on the last of it)
headline: sǐa!
scene: A kitchen at night lit only by an open fridge. A woman holds a prawn at arm's length over a bin with her face turned away, a tray of them on the counter beside her. Harsh white fridge light, dark room.

mnemonic: Set it down, and from that moment on: tâng, to set up, plus tɛ̀ɛ. The jar was stood on the trestle at dawn and has not moved since. Tâng-tɛ̀ɛ marks the point something started and kept going from. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the line running on from there)
headline: tâng-tɛ̀ɛ
scene: A market at dusk, stalls packed away, one bare wooden trestle left with a single heavy glass jar standing on it exactly where it was put. Empty aisle, litter, long orange shadows.

mnemonic: Slip a vowel into the middle of 'smart' and you have sǎa-mâat — and smart is exactly what it means: able to do the thing. A woman crouches at a dead fuse box and brings the stall back to life with a hairpin. (↓ falls on the second syllable, the job done)
headline: sǎa-mâat.
scene: A night market stall gone dark while the ones either side blaze. A woman crouches at an open fuse box with a hairpin between her fingers, the vendor holding a torch over her shoulder. Cables, crates, curious faces.

mnemonic: Outside plus from: nɔ̂ɔk, the knock at the door, and jàak, Jack with his suitcase. Everyone came except Jack, who never got past the step — apart from him, the party was complete. (▁ the last syllable settles low, the door stays shut)
headline: nɔ̂ɔk-jàak Jack
scene: A lit front room full of people seen through a window from the dark street, and one man standing outside on the path with a suitcase, looking in. Rain on the glass, his breath fogging, streetlight behind him.

mnemonic: A bowl of green curry lands in front of you and the cook asks whether you have ever had it. Say 'curry' with the R swallowed — kʰɤɤy — and that is the word: ever, have done before, used to. (— flat and level, an even question)
headline: kʰɤɤy?
scene: A bowl of green curry being set down in front of a diner by a smiling cook, steam lifting off it, rice and a spoon beside. Other diners at the long table lean in. Warm lamplight, worn wooden table.

mnemonic: A crow on the café railing caws at every table in turn until somebody gives up a chip. Kʰɔ̌ɔ is asking for — a favour, a discount, one more minute — and the voice climbs the way the caw does. (↑ rising, the call lifts at the end)
headline: kʰɔ̌ɔ…
scene: A seaside café terrace. A crow perched on the railing leans toward a table of chips with its beak open, wings half lifted, while two diners shield their plates with their forearms. Bright overcast light, gulls beyond.

mnemonic: The germ of an idea is the first version of it, before anybody improved it. Dɤɤm rhymes with germ and means exactly that: the original, the former, the way it was to start with. A gardener holds up the seed the whole orchard came from. (— flat and level, nothing has moved)
headline: dɤɤm.
scene: An old gardener's open palm holding one wrinkled seed, held out toward the viewer, with rows of heavy fruit trees receding behind him. Soil under his nails, morning light through the branches.

mnemonic: It comes in pairs: yîng this, yîng that — the more it rains, the more the lane floods. Rhyme it with king. One yîng sets the other going and both keep climbing. (↓ falling, though the meaning only goes up)
headline: yîng… yîng…
scene: A flooded narrow lane in heavy monsoon rain, a motorbike pushing a bow wave with water halfway up its wheels, the rider's feet lifted clear. Shophouses either side, rain bouncing off the surface.

mnemonic: The toddler's first word finally comes and the whole room stops dead. Kham sounds like 'come' and means word: one word, the unit you count them in. (— flat and level, a small even sound)
headline: kham.
scene: A living room. A toddler stands holding the edge of a chair with her mouth open mid-sound, and four adults around the room have frozen mid-movement, all turned toward her. Tea going cold, afternoon light.

mnemonic: Two old friends come round the same corner and nearly collide — pop, there he is, after fifteen years. Phóp is meeting someone, usually the kind of meeting you did not plan. (▲ high, the surprise snaps the voice up)
headline: phóp!
scene: Two men colliding at a busy street corner, bags dropped and spilling, both thrown back a step with their arms up and faces open in recognition. Pedestrians parting around them. Bright pavement, shopfronts.

mnemonic: The English article does the same job: an apple, an egg — one of a thing. ʔan is the all-purpose counter for small objects that have no classifier of their own. Point and say an, and the number of them follows. (— flat and level, a small unstressed word)
headline: ʔan nɯ̀ng
scene: A hardware stall counter with a shallow tray of identical small brass hinges. A customer's finger rests on exactly one of them; the stallholder's hand hovers ready to pick it out. Close crop, oily wood, warm bulb above.

mnemonic: Point at anything in the lane — the dog, the parked scooter, the pipe dripping on the step — and Thai calls it the same thing: man, said just like the English 'man'. It is 'it', and it does for animals and objects alike. (— flat and level, nothing special about it)
headline: man.
scene: A narrow lane with a sleeping dog, a leaning scooter and a dripping pipe all in frame, and a woman in the foreground gesturing loosely at the whole lot with one open hand. Washing overhead, hot flat light.

mnemonic: The mother word with the voice pushed up instead of dropped: mɛ̂ɛ is mother, mɛ́ɛ is even — even so, even though. A woman walks the whole way home in the rain even though the bus has passed her twice. (▲ high and taut, held up against the weather)
headline: mɛ́ɛ…
scene: A woman walking along a wet road under a small bent umbrella as a lit bus sweeps past her throwing spray, its windows full of dry passengers. Headlights, puddles, night.

mnemonic: A lifter at the bar takes one long breath — the lung fills and the power comes. Kam-lang is power, and it is also the word that puts a verb in the middle of happening: he is lifting, right now. (— both syllables flat, the effort held even)
headline: kam-lang.
scene: A weightlifter mid-lift in a bare gym, chest expanded, bar bending across his shoulders, chalk dust hanging in the light. Plates stacked against the wall, nobody else in the room.

mnemonic: The farmer lifts the wooden yoke off the buffalo's neck at the end of the day and the animal's head comes straight up. Yók is to lift, to raise — a glass, a hand, a price, a load. (▲ high, the voice comes up with the yoke)
headline: yók.
scene: A farmer lifting a heavy carved wooden yoke clear of a water buffalo's shoulders at dusk, the buffalo's head rising as the weight goes. Flooded paddy behind, orange sky, mud to the knee.

mnemonic: The opening note is the tone everything after it is tuned to, and a tree's trunk is where every branch starts. Tôn is that beginning — the start of the month, the stem of the plant, the first of a run. (↓ falling, the first note drops into the hall)
headline: tôn.
scene: A conductor's baton at the very top of its lift, the whole orchestra poised with bows raised and lips at mouthpieces, nobody yet playing. Dark hall beyond the stage lights.

mnemonic: The tow truck word on its own. Two cars hang off the same beam, one exactly as heavy as the other, and the beam sits level. Tʰâw is equal to, as much as — and it is how you say 'times' in a sum. (↓ falls hard, the hook taking the weight)
headline: tʰâw.
scene: A breakdown truck on a forecourt with a balance beam rigged from its crane, an identical small car hanging from each end, the beam perfectly level. Mechanics standing back with arms folded. Hard daylight.

mnemonic: Three syllables that end in a yam: phá-yaa-yaam. A boy hauls at a yam half out of baked ground, heels dug in and both hands on the leaves, and it will not come. Trying is the whole of the word. (— the last syllable levels out and runs on, like the effort)
headline: phá-yaa-yaam!
scene: A boy in a dry field leaning back at a steep angle with both hands gripping the leafy top of a half-exposed yam, heels dug into cracked soil. A basket waits empty beside him. Hard white sun.

mnemonic: Before anything stood here somebody sang it up: the foreman hums the shape of the roof and the frame goes up around him. Sâang is to build, to create, to make a thing exist. Stretch it — saaang. (↓ falling, the frame comes down onto its posts)
headline: sâang.
scene: Three builders hauling a timber house frame upright with ropes, one of them mid-song with his head back, sawdust hanging in the light. Half-laid floorboards, tools scattered, bright morning.

mnemonic: The night coach runs the whole lot of the way without stopping once — all night, no gap. Tà-lɔ̀ɔt is throughout: all night, all year, always, the stretch with nothing broken in it. (▁ both syllables low and flat, unbroken)
headline: tà-lɔ̀ɔt.
scene: A night coach seen from behind on an empty straight highway, tail lights receding, the road running dead ahead to a vanishing point under a sky full of stars. Dark fields either side.

mnemonic: Nǎng is hide — leather — and a book is what people wrote on before paper. Say 'sue' after it with the lips spread flat and you have nǎng-sǔɯ: a book, and by extension anything written down. (↑ both syllables climb, pages lifting)
headline: nǎng-sǔɯ.
scene: A thick leather-bound volume lying closed on a worn wooden table beside a rolled sheet of untanned hide and a bone stylus. One candle, deep shadow, grain visible in the leather.

mnemonic: The word kept for a judge, a monk or a minister — closer to 'sir' than to 'you'. It sounds like the 'than' in thank you, and thanking is about the right register: the clerk bows before every sentence. (↓ falling, the head dips with the voice)
headline: thâan.
scene: A panelled antechamber. A young clerk bows from the waist as he holds out a closed file with both hands to a robed elder who is reaching for it. Dark wood, brass lamp, one high window.

mnemonic: Not plus say: mâi, the flat refusal, and wâa, war with the R swallowed. No matter what anybody says — war, rain or ruin — the ferry leaves at six. (↓ both syllables drop, the decision already made)
headline: mâi wâa…
scene: A small wooden ferry pulling away from a jetty in heavy rain, the pilot facing forward, while three people on the jetty shout and wave after it with bags at their feet. Grey water, low cloud.

mnemonic: Forty moves come down to one pawn pushed onto the last rank. That single square is the result. Phǒn is the outcome of a thing — and also the fruit a tree produces. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as the piece goes forward)
headline: phǒn.
scene: A chessboard from low down: one lone pawn standing on the far rank, a king lying toppled beside it, two hands resting on the table edge either side. Wood grain, angled lamp light.

mnemonic: The pen from เป็น again, this time with clay in front of it. A lump on the wheel climbs into a bowl under the potter's hands while you watch it happen. Klaai-pen is to become — what a thing turns into. (— both syllables flat, the wheel turning evenly)
headline: klaai-pen.
scene: A potter's wheel spinning, two wet hands closing around a lump of grey clay that is rising into the walls of a bowl. Slip running down the wrists, water bucket beside, dim workshop light.

mnemonic: The man at the back of the queue has the longest wait of anybody. Lǎng is behind — the back of a thing, and after in time. Long queue, back of it, both in one word. (↑ rising, the voice climbs as he cranes to see the front)
headline: lǎng.
scene: An enormous queue snaking twice around a government building. The last man in line stands on tiptoe craning to see the distant front, bag on the ground at his feet. Hot sun, concrete, hundreds of shoulders.

mnemonic: Say LUKE with the lips pulled wide instead of pushed forward and you land lɯ̂ak. A sergeant walks the line, stops dead in front of one man and puts a finger on his chest: that one, chosen out of everybody. (↓ falling, the finger comes down on him)
headline: lɯ̂ak!
scene: A line of soldiers at attention on a parade ground, a sergeant halted in front of one and pressing a finger to his chest. The chosen man stares straight ahead. Dust, hard light, long row receding.

mnemonic: Something enormous flattened the field in the night and left one huge print in the mud. Nobody saw it. A giant ape, kʰong — probably. Kʰong is the hedge you put in front of a guess. (— flat and level, said with a shrug)
headline: kʰong.
scene: A flattened circle in a field of tall corn at dawn with one vast footprint pressed into the mud at its edge. Two farmers stand at the rim, one scratching his head, the other with hands on hips. Mist, grey light.

mnemonic: She does the whole tour on her own — no guide, no group, her own bag up all four hundred steps. Tua is the body, eeng is on its own: tua-eeng, oneself, by yourself, the self that did it. (— both syllables flat, an even climb)
headline: tua-eeng.
scene: A lone woman with a rucksack halfway up a long steep temple staircase flanked by carved serpent balustrades, empty steps above and below her. Morning haze, green trees, gold roof just visible at the top.

mnemonic: The tong from ต้อง with 'karn' after it. Wanting is a mild kind of must: the man in the flooded basement must have the tong, and the woman at the hardware counter tɔ̂ng-kaan a new pair. It is want with a spine in it. (— the second syllable levels out, the demand stated plainly)
headline: tɔ̂ng-kaan.
scene: A hardware shop counter. A woman holds up a pair of tongs snapped clean in half toward the shopkeeper, who is already turning to a wall of new ones. Racked tools floor to ceiling, strip lighting.

mnemonic: The magician slaps the table — dang — and whips the cloth away to show what was underneath it all along. Sà-dɛɛng is to show, to display, to perform. (— the second syllable holds flat and level, the reveal)
headline: sa-dɛɛng!
scene: A small stage. A magician sweeps a red cloth up and off a table, a brass birdcage revealed beneath it mid-flourish, the cloth still in the air. Footlights, dark auditorium, a few faces in the front row.

mnemonic: Put a hum in front of 'eye' and you have it: ngâai. An old woman threads a needle first go with one eye shut and hands it back to the girl who has been trying for ten minutes. Easy. (↓ falling, the hands drop as she finishes)
headline: ngâai.
scene: Close view of weathered hands holding a needle and thread just as the thread goes through, one eye squeezed shut. A young girl's hands wait open below. Sunlit doorway, sewing basket on a lap.

mnemonic: Rhymes with pie, with a J on the front. Thai puts this word inside every feeling: a cool jai is calm, a broken jai is heartbreak, a good jai is kind. Jai is the heart and the mind at once, sitting in the middle of the chest. (— flat and level, no movement in it)
headline: jai.
scene: A woman standing in a temple courtyard with one hand laid flat over her breastbone and her eyes closed, incense smoke drifting across her. Gold stupa blurred behind, early light.

mnemonic: Six teenagers packed under one shop awning in the rain, shoulders touching, all in the gloom together. Klùm is a group — the huddle, the bunch, the lot of them. (▁ low and flat, nobody moving)
headline: klùm.
scene: Six teenagers crammed under a narrow shop awning in heavy rain, shoulders pressed together, bags held over heads. Grey street, water sheeting off the awning edge, closed shutters behind them.

mnemonic: The father word with the drop taken out: pʰɔ̂ɔ is dad, pʰɔɔ is enough. His enormous paw goes flat over the top of the glass before anyone can pour more. Same paw, level voice. (— flat and level, no drop at all)
headline: phɔɔ.
scene: A dinner table. A big weathered hand lies flat across the mouth of a glass while a bottle tips toward it and stops. Plates pushed back, other hands resting on the cloth. Warm evening light.

mnemonic: The doorman looks at one face after another and says nah to each of them. Nâa is the face — and also the front of anything: the front of the queue, the front of a shirt, the week in front of this one. (↓ falling, flat refusal straight to the face)
headline: nâa.
scene: A club doorway at night. A doorman's flat palm rests against the chest of the next man in line while he looks past him at the others. Red lamp above the door, velvet rope, faces in the queue.

mnemonic: A boy at the paint counter prises the lid off one tin after another to see what is actually inside each one, because colour is the thing you can only know by looking. Sǐi is colour, and it sounds exactly like 'see'. (↑ rising, the lid comes up)
headline: sǐi.
scene: A hardware shop paint counter. A boy levers the lid off a tin of bright blue paint with a screwdriver, a row of already-opened tins of different colours beside him, lids stacked. Bright shop light.

mnemonic: A bin lid goes over on the tiles at two in the morning — dang — and the whole street knows about it. Dang is loud, and a person who is dang is famous for exactly the same reason. (— flat and level, the noise hanging on)
headline: dang!
scene: A metal bin lid spinning to a stop on dark courtyard tiles, a cat streaking away from the overturned bin, and two upstairs windows lighting up. Night, wet stone, one bare bulb over a door.

mnemonic: Say 'summer' the British way with the R swallowed, and push the end up: sà-mɤ̌ɤ. Summer always comes back, every single year, whether anyone asks for it or not. Sà-mɤ̌ɤ is always. (↑ rising, the last syllable climbs like the heat)
headline: sà-mɤ̌ɤ.
scene: A village pond dried back to cracked mud at its edges, three children paddling in the shallow middle of what is left, a buffalo lying in the shade. Hard white sunlight, dry trees, no cloud.

mnemonic: Eight in the morning and the whole country stands still for one song. Say 'chart' with the R swallowed and you have châat: the nation — and also a whole lifetime, this one and the next one along. (↓ falling, the flag reaches the top as the voice drops)
headline: châat.
scene: A school yard at morning assembly: rows of children standing rigid facing a flagpole, a flag halfway up, two older pupils at the rope. Long shadows across the concrete, low sun.

mnemonic: Rian is lean and learn in one word: the boy at the back is bent so far over his desk that his nose is nearly on the page. Rian is to study, and Thais themselves often say the r as an l. (— flat and level, the long hours)
headline: rian.
scene: A classroom at dusk with every desk empty but one. A boy is bent right down over his desk, nose almost touching it, a small lamp beside him. Chalk dust, shuttered windows, blue light outside.

mnemonic: Roong is the big shed you put a thing inside: roong plus study is a school, roong plus film is a cinema, roong plus sick is the hospital. Say it like 'wrong' with the o drawn out. (— flat and level, a plain roof over everything)
headline: roong.
scene: A long corrugated-iron hall at the edge of a town, doors standing open at both ends so daylight shows straight through, bicycles leaning along its side wall. Dust, palms, hard midday sun.

mnemonic: Say 'chew' with the lips spread flat and let it fall away into 'ah': chɯ̂a. A woman is told the plank bridge will hold and steps onto it anyway. Believing is doing it before you know. (↓ falling, the foot comes down)
headline: chɯ̂a.
scene: A woman putting her weight onto the first plank of a rope-and-board bridge over a misty gorge, one hand gripping the rope, the other out for balance. Boards missing further along. Cold grey light.

mnemonic: The decorator dabs a mark of paint along the wall at exactly the height of his string line, each dab level with the last one. Rá-dàp is the level: the grade, the rank, the height a thing has got to. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the dab lands)
headline: rá-dàp.
scene: A bare room being decorated. A hand dabs paint onto a wall in a row of small marks that follow a taut string line pinned across it. Ladder, dust sheets, open tin on the floor. Flat daylight.

mnemonic: Pert, like the shop that opens dead on time with its shutter snapped up in one movement. Bpɤ̀ɤt rhymes with pert and means to open — a door, a shop, a bottle, a switch. (▁ low and flat, the shutter goes up in one go)
headline: bpɤ̀ɤt.
scene: A shopkeeper rolling a metal shutter up above his head in one sweep, the dark shop interior appearing beneath it. Empty street, awning half unfurled, first pale light down the road.

mnemonic: Say 'lure' with the lips spread flat and lift it: lɯ̌a. One prawn is left on the plate and nobody will take it, sitting there as a lure for whoever gives in first. Lɯ̌a is what is left over. (↑ rising, the voice lifts on the last one)
headline: lɯ̌a.
scene: A nearly bare serving plate in the middle of a crowded table with one prawn left on it, four hands hovering nearby without committing. Empty shells, crumpled napkins, beer glasses, warm light.

mnemonic: A mongoose up on its hind legs, absolutely still, eyes fixed on one point in the grass. Mɔɔng is that: looking at something, holding your eyes on it rather than merely seeing it. (— flat and level, the stare held steady)
headline: mɔɔng.
scene: A mongoose standing upright on a termite mound, head and eyes locked on one spot in dry grass below, body rigid. Low golden light, long shadow, scrub stretching away behind.

mnemonic: Every relative in the province is in the yard: forty of them on plastic chairs, and you are introduced to all forty. Yâat is a relative, said like 'yard' with the R swallowed. (↓ falling, the introductions keep coming)
headline: yâat.
scene: A crowded courtyard of plastic chairs packed with dozens of people of all ages dressed in white under a marquee, a young man being led along a row shaking hands. Hot afternoon, fans, tea urns.

mnemonic: A tit — the small bird — clamps onto the fat ball hanging from the branch and hangs there upside down for an hour, refusing to let go. Tìt is stuck to, attached to, caught on, addicted to. (▁ low and flat, clamped on)
headline: tìt.
scene: A small blue and yellow bird clinging upside down to a hanging fat ball on a bare winter branch, wings tight to its body, claws locked. Frost on the twigs, pale garden behind.

mnemonic: Try getting a yak up a hill it does not fancy. It plants four feet and the entire expedition stops where it stands. Yâak is difficult — the long drawn yaaak of an animal that will not move. (↓ falling, the voice drops with the load)
headline: yâak.
scene: A loaded yak standing immovable on a steep stony mountain path, two guides hauling on a rope from above with their heels dug in. Thin cold air, prayer flags, snow peaks behind.

mnemonic: An old post room where every canister goes bop into its brass tube and lands in the right room three floors away. Rá-bòp is the system: the works, the way the parts fit together. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the canister lands)
headline: rá-bòp.
scene: A sorting room walled with brass pneumatic tubes, one canister dropping into a wire basket while a clerk in shirtsleeves reaches for it. Other clerks at benches, dusty light from high windows.

mnemonic: Three flat pats and a long last note: phát-thá-naa. A man pats wet concrete smooth over what was a dirt lane, and by evening the lane is a road. Phatthanaa is to develop — the word on every notice about progress. (— the last syllable levels out long and flat)
headline: phát-thá-naa.
scene: A man crouched on a plank laid over fresh wet concrete, patting and smoothing the surface with a float, the unfinished dirt lane still visible ahead of him. Neighbours watching from doorways, late sun.

mnemonic: English has half of it already: you don't know jack. Rúu is to know and jàk finishes it — rúu-jàk is knowing a person, being acquainted. Two men shake hands at a party and find they grew up on the same lane. (▁ the second syllable drops low, the handshake lands)
headline: rúu-jàk!
scene: Two middle-aged men gripping each other's hand at a crowded party, both leaning back with their free hands on each other's shoulders, mouths open in recognition. Drinks abandoned on a sideboard, warm light.

mnemonic: A toddler gets hold of the photographer's lens cap and within a minute it is a spinning top, a wheel and a hat. Lên is to play — with a toy, a sport, an instrument, or anything that was not a toy until now. (↓ falling, the cap lands and spins)
headline: lên.
scene: A toddler sitting on a wooden floor spinning a large black lens cap like a top, an open camera bag beside her and a camera body just out of reach. Afternoon light across the boards.
